text:
Rafael Mendes: heads up — looking at canary data from last night’s spike. our `Retry-After` values are basically always `1` right now. it’s… not great. clients are hammering and we’re seeing mini retry storms.

Rafael Mendes: question for this thread: can we tune `Retry-After` to better match observed recovery time when breakers open / admission sheds? ideally something deterministic + customer-actionable.

Christine Wong: yup. i pulled some quick stats from breaker transitions (us-east, 2 models in canary). when breaker opens due to pool saturation, time-to-half-open is typically >5s.

Christine Wong: rough percentiles from logs:
```
open_duration_seconds
p50: 6.8s
p90: 18.4s
p99: 43.1s
```
so telling people “retry in 1s” guarantees they slam us while we’re still open.

Tomáš Novák: +1. also our edge admission shed for queue depth is usually short-lived (sub-second to a couple seconds) but breaker-open is a longer cool down.

Allison Grant: we should be careful: `Retry-After` semantics in HTTP allow either seconds or HTTP date. we should stick to integer seconds everywhere for sanity + sdk consistency.

Brian Murphy: current behavior in PR-18421 sets `Retry-After: 1` for any overload-mapped response (429/503) because we didn’t want to block people too long.

Brian Murphy: but agreed: it’s misleading. also OpenAI-compat clients tend to respect the header if present. when absent they just do their own exponential backoff (often without jitter :/).

Monica Patel: from SDK side: we already surface `Retry-After` in python/ts/go errors. but customers still implement their own loops. if header says 1s they’ll do 1s repeatedly (and not apply exponential).

Ibrahim Khan: + our docs draft says “respect Retry-After; otherwise exponential backoff with jitter”. but ppl will follow the header literally.

Sergio Costa: do we want a single value across all overload reasons, or different values per reason code? i worry about exposing too much internal detail but reason codes are already part of the response payload.

Christine Wong: i’m in favor of per-reason (or per-layer) *as long as* it’s still stable.
- `ROUTING_BREAKER_OPEN`: should reflect cooldown/half-open schedule
- `EDGE_ADMISSION_QUEUE_FULL`: short (1–2s)
- `RUNTIME_MEMORY_PRESSURE`: medium (5–10s) because pressure tends to clear slower

Amara Diallo: gateway can set header based on the reason it’s returning. but in some cases it’s coming back from routing/runtime and we just map it. we can plumb through a suggested retry from downstream.

Rafael Mendes: would prefer we don’t invent different behavior in 3 places. can we define a single source of truth rule?

Christine Wong: routing breaker can compute an explicit `retry_after_seconds` when open. it already knows the `opened_at`, `cooldown`, and next probe time. so for breaker-open cases, we can set:
`Retry-After = max(1, ceil(next_probe_ts - now))`

Christine Wong: that makes it deterministic and aligned with hysteresis.

Allison Grant: +1. if we do that, we also need to watch for cardinality/label explosion in metrics if we start bucketing by retry_after. but header itself is fine.

Tomáš Novák: for edge admission (queue depth), we don’t have a “next probe” concept. but we can still choose a sane default based on observed recovery. what are we seeing?

Sergio Costa: from dashboard: queue-depth shedding events clear fast. when shed-rate spikes, it usually stabilizes within ~2–4s unless it’s actually a breaker-open scenario.

Rafael Mendes: so suggestion:
- breaker-open: dynamic based on routing state
- edge shed (local queue full): fixed 2s
- runtime shed (bounded queue / scheduler): fixed 2s? maybe 3s?

Brian Murphy: product angle: we should keep it simple in docs. “If you receive 429/503 with `Retry-After`, wait at least that many seconds, then retry with exponential backoff + jitter.”

Monica Patel: important detail: “wait at least” is good. customers can still add jitter on top.

Ibrahim Khan: we should explicitly recommend jitter even when honoring header. something like:
`wait = retry_after * random(1.0, 1.3)`
so clients don’t synchronize.

Allison Grant: +1. and cap max backoff. otherwise long outages lead to super long delays but also weird traffic patterns when they all wake up.

Christine Wong: breaker-open p99 ~43s. do we really want to tell clients to wait 43s? seems high.

Rafael Mendes: if the breaker is open for 43s, that’s reality. but maybe we cap what we *advertise*? i’m conflicted.

Tomáš Novák: capping advertised retry can be counterproductive. if we cap at 10s while breaker stays open 40s, clients will retry 4x during open window.

Brian Murphy: also consistent with “customer-actionable”. if we’re overloaded for 40s, better to tell them.

Amara Diallo: another nuance: streaming requests. if they reconnect aggressively we get hammered in handshake + prefill. a longer retry_after during breaker-open is actually helpful.

Sergio Costa: could we clamp only for weird edge cases (like >120s) and otherwise report real probe time? and we can still “probe early” internally with a small percent of traffic.

Christine Wong: breaker design already does small probe in half-open. we don’t need clients to probe for us.

Rafael Mendes: ok, i’m leaning:
1) dynamic `Retry-After` for breaker-open (routing computed, gateway forwards)
2) fixed `Retry-After: 2` for queue-full shed and runtime shed
3) docs/sdk guidance: honor header, add jitter, exponential for repeated failures, max retries, etc.

Monica Patel: for SDK examples, propose:
- attempt 1: wait retry_after (+ jitter)
- if it fails again with overload: wait `max(retry_after, base * 2^n)` with jitter, cap at 30s
- stop after N retries or total elapsed > 2min

Ibrahim Khan: + and emphasize idempotency / safe retries. for non-streaming chat/completions it’s usually ok if they’re not doing side effects. for tool calls it can be tricky.

Brian Murphy: in the API error payload we already include `code` + `type=overload`. we can add `retry_after` in JSON too? (OpenAI compat sometimes includes it)

Allison Grant: if we include it, make it redundant with header, not the only source. header is canonical.

Incident Bot: (context) Incident INC-21407 summary posted in #incidents: overload in us-east, breaker open ~22s, shed rate peaked at 14%. (reactions: :eyes: 4)

Rafael Mendes: ^ this is exactly the example. breaker open 22s, but we told clients 1s.

Christine Wong: i can wire `retry_after_seconds` into the breaker evaluation response and have gateway set header accordingly when reason = `ROUTING_BREAKER_OPEN`.

Amara Diallo: gateway side: doable. we already branch on reason code for metrics. just need to plumb the value and ensure it’s present on both REST + OpenAI-compat endpoints.

Sergio Costa: do we need to adjust alerting/SLO accounting if we change retry_after? (customers might see fewer attempts but longer recovery)

Tomáš Novák: SLO side: no change in classification; these are still overload-protected errors. but we should watch customer ticket volume. messaging matters.

Brian Murphy: also need to ensure `Retry-After` is always set for overload-protected errors. today some 503s from upstream timeouts don’t include it.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. if we’re returning 503 due to *overload shedding*, set it. if it’s an internal 503, we should *not* lie.

Allison Grant: + make sure we don’t include Retry-After on non-overload 5xx. otherwise clients will treat internal bugs as retryable and hide issues.

Monica Patel: can we also update SDK retry helper to apply jitter even when header is present? i can take that as an action.

Ibrahim Khan: i’ll update the code snippets in docs + SDK examples. right now they show “sleep(retry_after)” without jitter.

Christine Wong: proposal for fixed defaults:
- `EDGE_ADMISSION_QUEUE_FULL`: 2s
- `RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL`: 2s
- `RUNTIME_KV_CACHE_PRESSURE`: 5s (tends to recover slower)
- `ROUTING_BREAKER_OPEN`: dynamic (next probe)

Rafael Mendes: ok. let’s do that. 

Rafael Mendes: action items:
- Christine: add dynamic retry_after to routing breaker response + tests
- Amara/Brian: gateway mapping: set header based on reason + propagate routing-provided value
- Monica/Ibrahim: SDK + docs: “wait at least Retry-After, add jitter; exponential backoff for repeated overload; cap/backstop”
- Sergio/Allison: add panel tracking retry_after distribution + correlate with breaker open duration (to validate we’re not lying)

Sergio Costa: +1. i’ll add a quick panel: `retry_after_seconds` histogram for overload responses (sampled) and overlay breaker open duration.

Allison Grant: note on sampling: don’t put raw retry_after as a label. use log sampling or histogram buckets.

Tomáš Novák: once this ships, we should watch for customers doing “retry forever” loops. support tickets SUP-3974 type.

Rafael Mendes: yep. we’ll add explicit “max retries / cap total retry time” guidance in support doc.

Brian Murphy: i’ll also confirm OpenAI-compat clients are ok with larger Retry-After. some libraries treat >60s weirdly.

Christine Wong: if we see >60s often, that’s a bigger capacity incident anyway. but we can monitor.

Rafael Mendes: cool. thanks all. let’s aim to get this into next canary push so we can see if shed-rate smooths out and retries drop.
